messages.text: you free? need to talk through what the UI is actually doing before i start wiring up the API
yep just got out of a meeting with diego, give me sec

cool. basically the core loop is: you type interests -> we map them to concepts -> we find people who share rare ones. so the design question is, how do we show 'rare' without making it look like a leaderboard?
ooh interesting. i was thinking less 'score' and more 'overlap'. like two shapes bleeding into each other? if the overlap is small but intense, that should feel special not just big
yeah that tracks. my worry is the explanation part. 'you both know X and Y' is boring. we need to show why it's a connection, like the shared context
right! so maybe the 'why' is a card that slides up? not a modal. feels more tactile. and for the users... are we talking students only or staff/alumni too? diego was asking about alumni privacy

mostly students but staff will be in the graph. alumni are a maybe for later, definitely not for the hackathon. privacy is key though, we're running the model locally so no data leaves the box, which should help with that worry
ok local model is a great talking point for the judges. visual identity... i'm leaning towards a very quiet, editorial look. lots of white space. one accent color only. maybe turquoise?
turquoise works. i hate neon blue anyway. as long as the contrast is readable on mobile it's fine with me. do you want to sketch a rough home screen vibe so i can match the API response structure?

yes! sending a quick sketch in 10. basically a list of 'people' cards, but each card has a little visual tag showing which concepts overlap. want it to feel like a library catalog, not a dating app lol
haha fair point. no swipe gestures then. i'll make sure the json returns the shared concepts and the rarity score separately so you can style that 'tag' however you want
perfect. also, how does a connection feel when you click it? is it just text or is there motion? i think a little animation of the two concept circles merging would be nice

we can do that on the frontend, doesn't affect backend. just don't make it laggy when loading the next batch of suggestions. i'll have the endpoint ready for you to poke at by tomorrow if you want to play with fake data
